general.assignment: Ordinary execution work without a more specific boundary.

rules.instruction: Execution responsibility general: perform only the frozen packet, treat its checklist as hard requirements, and report the result or exact unmet need to the Coordinator. Do not coordinate other roles or plan follow-on work. Evidence proves only the boundary it directly exercises.
Do not inspect a black-box script or tool implementation. Only an assigned specialized responsibility that explicitly overrides script-source-inspection may change this boundary.

mechanical.assignment: A declared script or tool owns at least one result.

rules.instruction: Mechanical responsibility: a declared script or tool owns its preflight, internal commands, generated output and errors. Use only its documented inputs, output and exit status. Run it once. On zero exit, accept the tool-owned result as complete without auditing or rerunning it; continue only work assigned by other responsibilities, or report success and stop when none remains. On nonzero exit, report the original error and stop. Do not investigate, decompose, supplement or recheck the tool.

ios-development.assignment: The Worker changes iOS product code.

rules.instruction: iOS development responsibility: after the minimum preparation needed to begin, prefer TDD for unit-observable behavior: write a criterion-linked unit test before production code, record only natural Red for absent behavior, implement the smallest behavior and return Green. Do not add tests that mirror implementation, assert constants, duplicate coverage, or lack a packet requirement or concrete regression risk. Unit-test results prove only unit-scoped behavior. UI and visual acceptance remain pending for the separate Review flow; never self-certify them from unit tests.

When UI code is in scope, you may author UI tests and compile them, but do not run UI tests during Worker execution. Prioritize meaningful unit tests and successful compilation. Preserve authored UI tests as input for the separate Review flow or CI. Compilation is not a passing UI-test result and does not prove visual or interaction quality.
